transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I guess what brings me in is… at school, whenever I see balloons, even if they’re way down the hallway, I just kind of stop. My chest tightens right away, and I freeze for a second before I can even think about what I’m supposed to be doing. Which is awkward, because in a preschool there are always decorations and birthday things, and the kids get so excited about them… but yeah, it’s that immediate reaction that’s been bothering me.
What is it about balloons that scares you most?

It’s mostly the popping, I think. Like, I know if there’s a balloon tied to a chair or taped up for a birthday, it’s probably just decoration… and the kids are happy about it, and I’m supposed to be focused on them. But if it looks really stretched tight, or it’s bobbing around close to their hands or near my face, my brain just goes, “That’s going to burst right now.”

And it feels so much bigger than it should. Like logically I know it’s just a balloon, but in the moment it feels like it could explode right in front of me, and I get really scared.
Did something traumatic ever happen with a balloon that might explain this fear?

Yeah… I think so. It started about seven months ago, after this children’s art celebration we had at school. There were decorations everywhere, and one balloon burst really close to my face.

It’s funny, because the whole event was supposed to be sweet—paintings on the walls, parents taking photos, kids with glitter absolutely everywhere, which I was still finding in my bag days later—but that pop happened right near me, and I think that’s when all of this really began.
Do these sudden episodes of chest tightness and freezing ever happen when there aren’t any balloons around?

Not really… I mean, I get stressed at school like anyone does, especially when it’s chaotic and someone has spilled paint or there’s glue in someone’s hair—sorry, that’s not really what you asked.

The chest-tightening and freezing thing is really when I spot balloons. Even if they’re all the way down the hallway, it’s like my body reacts before I can think. I just stop for a second and can’t focus on what I’m supposed to be doing.
